source: 1-loop electroweak box, alternating W/Z mass propagators, 4 distinct kinematic invariants {s, t, mWsq, mZsq}.  Phase 3 oracle for the multi-invariant axis (ROADMAP row 'Invariants ≥3: electroweak s, t, m_W, m_Z').  Family layout: 4 propagators (W,Z,W,Z) with 4 massless external legs.  At s = 7, t = -3, mWsq = 1, mZsq = 4/3 the WW bubble (s = 7 > 4mW^2 = 4) is above threshold, so j[ewbox, 1,0,1,0] and j[ewbox, 1,1,1,0]/[1,1,1,1] carry physical imaginary parts.

cpp_sampled_status.result: completed and matches Mathematica reference at rel ~10⁻³⁰ across all 7 sampled values (corner j[ewbox,1,1,1,1] + 6 sub-masters: W/Z tadpoles, WW/ZZ bubbles, WZW/WZZ triangles).  First oracle for the Phase 3 multi-invariant axis (4 distinct kinematic invariants {s, t, mWsq, mZsq}); no audit divergence surfaced — the multi-invariant code paths (kira_yaml.cpp's mass_scale_names + kira_run.cpp's -s emission + libp_deriv multi-invariant chain rule) work end-to-end.
cpp_sampled_status.note: All 7 sampled values pass at rel ≤ 4 × 10⁻³⁰ (well within the project's standard ~10⁻³⁰ tolerance).  C++ wallclock 39 s vs MMA 62 s; C++ is faster at 1-loop scale.  The j[ewbox,1,1,0,1] imag part shows rel ≈ 2.7 × 10⁻⁷ but abs ≈ 7 × 10⁻⁷¹, i.e. both MMA and C++ agree the integral is real to ~64 digits of precision (numerical noise floor) — compare_sampled.py accepts this via the abs-tol gate.  Compare via tools/bench/compare_sampled.py.
